jen: heads up — ran the long-context perf suite overnight and saw steady memory growth on kv-cache instances. not a leak per se, looks like fragmentation + many tiny live blocks.
omar: can you share numbers? what size and workload? :thinking:
sylvia: quick summary from the run: baseline (seq=8k) stable ~28GB. longcontext (seq=16k, 2M tokens) climbs 28GB -> 36.5GB over 6h. small-block count (<=128B) increases x3, free-list fragments up.
jen: repro steps i used: `./run_longcontext.sh --model rdx-tiny --batch 8 --seq 16000 --duration 6h`
jen: added heap snapshot at 0h/3h/6h, attached diffs to the perf bucket (link: https://perf.internal/kv/1805/longcontext-overnight)
kevin: looked at the pprof. pattern is allocator holding many 64B/128B chunks tagged by kv-entry refs. eviction triggers but we keep short-lived prefixes pinned in the KV LRU which prevents consolidation.
sylvia: allocator details: we use slab buckets [64,128,256,512,1024,...]. current heuristic rounds up to next power-of-two bucket. fragmentation especially from 96B-ish entries going into 128B bucket.
omar: so two knobs: bucket granularity and compaction cadence. which should we try first?
kevin: quick experiment idea: add an intermediate 96B bucket and enable a low-priority background compactor that merges adjacent free slots in same slab. no global stop-the-world.
jen: also saw lots of reclaimed KV entries staying in an LRU 'ghost' ring for ~10s before eviction — increases transient peak. we could be more aggressive with ghost eviction under memory pressure.
sylvia: i sketched a config change: `kv.alloc.buckets = [48, 64, 96, 128, 192, 256, 384, 512]` and `kv.compactor.max-cpu = 0.05` to keep compaction backgroundy.
kevin: that bucket list is promising. edge-case: CPU vs throughput tradeoff — background compaction will consume cycles during high-throughput bursts. need a dynamic throttle tied to recent p50 latency delta.
omar: would be nice to gate compaction if p50 increases > 5ms. something like: `if p50_latency_delta > 5ms then pause compactor for 30s`
jen: we should also log compaction work units and fragmentation reduction metrics. current telemetry only emits total_free_bytes and free_chunks; add `fragmentation_ratio` and `compactions_inflight` to console.
sylvia: agreed. i can add the metrics patch. kevin — can you prototype the small-bucket + compactor in a branch? try to replicate the night run with that branch.
kevin: i'll spin up a canary with `kv-buckets-experiment` branch and run the same workload. ETA EOD.
jen: if we see >20% drop in steady-state memory for longcontext runs, we can land. otherwise next step is aggressive ghost eviction + opportunistic merge on free-list allocation.
omar: one more thought — kernel selection / batching interplay: larger batches increase KV sharing (good for reuse) but also increase simultaneous live KV entries (bad for peak). we should add a test matrix: batch={1,4,8}, seq={8k,16k} and measure mem/throughput/latency.
sylvia: adding that to the perf plan. i will create a lightweight dashboard with the new fragmentation_ratio metric. link when ready.
eng-runtime-bot: deploy-notice: canary infra with `kv-buckets-experiment` scheduled at 2023-10-12T03:00Z to 2023-10-12T09:00Z — monitor `kv.fragmentation_ratio` and `p50_latency`.
jen: thanks — let's reconvene after the canary results. quick sync tomorrow 11:00.
kevin: ack — will post logs + flamegraphs. :mag:
omar: thanks everyone. this feels actionable. :thumbsup:
